Hi Ellie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a one-page term summary that sketches the structure Redwood would support for an annual prepay with an optional multi-year discount. High-level proposal:

- Deal: 3-year commitment, upfront prepay for Year 1 + Year 2 (Year 3 option at renewal).
- Yearly tiers: Year 1 (baseline) -> Year 2 (10% uplift tiered discount) -> Year 3 (voluntary renewal at a 5% renewal credit if exercised).
- Ramp schedule: milestone-based ramp to full usage over 12 months (0% in month 0 -> 40% months 1–3 -> 75% months 4–8 -> 100% month 9+). We can extend to 18–24 months if needed.
- Early termination / refund waterfall (draft): 80% refund of unused prepaid dollars in Year 1 (less administrative fee), 50% in Year 2, 0% in Year 3. Refunds are subject to simple amortization to avoid double-counting credits.
- Co-terming: option A — convert remaining prepay to a monthly credit at a discounted rate to align to Nimbus's existing September 2027 co-term; option B — keep prepaid schedule and apply pro-rated credit at renewal.

Attachments: Redwood_Term_Summary_v3.pdf (term bullets + example waterfall).

Next steps: please flag the items you want tightened (refund %, ramp length, liability cap) and we will run numbers from finance. Happy to set a short working session next week with Lauren & Vivek to go line by line.

Monica —

Thanks for the write-up and the call recap. A few immediate questions from procurement and finance:

1) Refund mechanics: we prefer a milestone-based refund (for example, full refund less usage through the later of actual consumption or an agreed ramp curve). Your 80%/50%/0% bands are a good starting point but we need clarity on day-0 -> month-by-month calculations and an administrative fee cap.

2) Co-terming: Nimbus has an existing enterprise agreement that runs to 2027-09. We need the ability to align the Redwood contract to that date so we don't pay double during overlap. Can you propose exact conversion math?

3) Liability cap & escrow: procurement would like prepaid amounts to sit in a simple escrow/reserve with a clear trigger for refund release. Also need to see liability cap language — ideally limited to the prepaid amount.

4) Ramp duration: we'll push to extend the ramp to 18 months given product rollout timing.

Please send a worked example of the refund waterfall (line items showing $numbers) — that will accelerate legal and finance review. If you can include an escrow vs amortization comparison that would be ideal.

Ellie / team —

Appreciate the quick feedback. I've sketched two operationally realistic mechanisms below and attached to this thread I'll follow up with a sample CSV: scenario A (escrow reserve) and scenario B (amortized credit). High-level: both protect you vs. overpayment; they differ on timing and bookkeeping.

Scenario A — Escrow reserve
- Nimbus prepays Years 1+2 into an escrow account managed by a neutral custodian.
- Refund trigger: 6 months' notice for termination; escrow releases pro-rated balance for unused months less a 3% administrative fee.
- Co-terming: escrow can be applied to bridge to September 2027; remaining balance converts to monthly credits at your discounted rate.

Scenario B — Amortized credit (finance-friendly)
- Prepay is amortized monthly across the committed term on Redwood's books. If termination occurs, remaining unamortized balance is refunded per waterfall percentages (80% first year, etc.) but the refund is net of amortized usage credits. No third-party escrow required.

Example (illustrative only):
- Upfront prepay: $1,200,000 for Year 1 + Year 2 commitment (covers expected ramp).
- Ramp to 100% in 12 months (we can model 18 months): if termination at month 8, unamortized balance = $500k -> refund = 80% * $500k = $400k (Scenario B) or escrow release = pro-rated less admin fee (Scenario A).

On co-terming math: two operational options
1) Align immediately: remaining prepaid dollars converted to monthly credit at (prepaid $ / remaining months to 2027-09) and applied to invoices.
2) Hold as renewal credit: remaining prepaid dollars kept as a renewal credit with a 12-month expiry from co-term date.

I recommend Scenario B for speed to close (no third-party escrow) and offer a 3-point concession: increase Year 1 refund to 85% for termination in the first 6 months, hold liability cap equal to prepaid amount. That should address finance while keeping operational friction low.

I'll attach a CSV with 3 worked waterfalls (12m ramp, 18m ramp, 24m ramp).

- Vivek
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
